qt: to the Commission Barbara Bonte (PfE) Subject:

Version 5.2 of the Belgian Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund (AMIF) programme, approved by Implementing Decision C(2026)6201 of 22 July 2026, provides that the new Dublin centre is to be funded using the resources remaining in the general AMIF envelope and the national budget. Compared to version 4.0, this means an increase in the indicative Union contribution to reception conditions from EUR 18.93 million to EUR 49.76 million and in the target for newly created reception places from 0 to 320. The announced centre in Nazareth-De Pinte will have around 300 places and will be set up in rented private hotel facilities. 1.

In Belgium’s reasoned request for amendment under Article 24(1) of Regulation (EU) 2021/1060, what justification did it provide for the increase in resources for reception conditions, and what amount was envisaged for the funding of the new Dublin centre?
Does the increase in the target from 0 to 320 reception places relate entirely or partially to this centre?

On what legal basis under Regulation (EU) 2021/1147 did the Commission consider the AMIF funding for this centre to be compatible with the Fund, and under what conditions are rental costs for such private facilities eligible for AMIF funding?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.11.2026) In 2025, the Commission allocated additional funding resources, including under the Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund (AMIF)1, to support Member States with the implementation of the Pact on Migration and Asylum (the Pact2) and the management of temporary protection3. The amendment introduced by Implementing Decision C (2026)6201 of 22 July 2026 concerns extra funding given to Belgium to help prepare for and implement the Pact. Part of this funding is to be used to strengthen the Belgian asylum system, including improving reception conditions in line with the new provisions of the Pact. The amendment does not provide further details about individual projects. According to the information available to the Commission, places for applicants for international protection in Belgium waiting to be transferred to the Member State responsible for their case are also included in the reception places target, which was increased by the amendment. One of the AMIF objectives is to contribute to strengthening and developing all aspects of the Common European Asylum System, including the reinforcement of Member States’ reception capacity, where necessary4. In accordance with Article 63 of Regulation (EU) 2021/10605, expenditure eligibility is determined on the basis of national rules, except where specific rules are laid down in that Regulation or the AMIF Regulation.
